issues.legal_issue: The valuation method prescribed by municipal bye-laws governs property-tax assessments made after those bye-laws take effect, rather than earlier judicial principles developed for assessments constrained by rent-control legislation.
material_facts: The municipal corporation had enacted bye-laws prescribing how annual rent and rateable value were to be determined.
The assessments in issue concerned periods after those bye-laws came into force.
The earlier judicial principles relied on by the taxpayers had been developed in cases involving premises governed by rent-control legislation.
The High Court had applied those earlier principles despite the existence of the municipal corporation’s valuation bye-laws.
issues.conclusion: Assessments made after the 1994 bye-laws came into force must be governed by those bye-laws, and the principles in the earlier rent-control cases do not govern those assessments.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116(1) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act sets the general measure of rateable value, while bye-law 3 of the 1994 Bye-Laws prescribes how annual rent is determined. Where the municipal legislation itself provides a method for determining annual value, that method governs rather than a rent-control statute’s fair-rent or standard-rent limit. The Court relied on Assistant General Manager, Central Bank of India v. Commissioner, Municipal Corporation for the City of Ahmedabad, East India Commercial Company Private Limited v. Corporation of Calcutta, and The Commissioner v. Griha Yajamanula Samkhya; it distinguished The Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Debi, Dr. Balbir Singh v. Municipal Corporation, Delhi, and Lt. Col. P.R. Chaudhary v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, which concerned assessments in the context of rent-control legislation. It also noted that Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Delhi Urban House Owners’ Welfare Association had upheld the bye-laws.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns the assessment of property tax on land or a building by a municipal authority.
predicates.assessment_after_valuation_bylaws: The assessment concerns a period after the municipal authority’s valuation bye-laws took effect.
predicates.bylaws_prescribe_valuation_method: The municipal authority’s bye-laws prescribe how the relevant annual value or rent is to be determined.

issues.definition: When a municipal property-tax assessment concerns a period after applicable valuation bye-laws took effect and those bye-laws prescribe the valuation method, the assessment must follow those bye-laws.

issues.legal_issue: An assessee may seek assessment under the new annual-value method for a pre-change property-tax assessment that remains unresolved or is pending in an appeal covered by the transitional provisions.
material_facts: A 2003 amendment introduced an annual-value method based on unit area values and provided for self-assessment.
The amendment included a transitional provision for assessments that had not been finalized when it came into force.
It also provided for appeals pending before a District Judge to be transferred to the Municipal Taxation Tribunal if an applicant requested disposal on the basis of annual value.
The High Court treated an assessment set aside and remanded for redetermination as not finalized.
The Supreme Court held that the term “settlement” in the appeal provision meant a determination by the Tribunal, not a consensual arrangement between the parties.
The Court held that the new method could be selected at the appellate stage even for an assessment year before the amendment, and that unresolved remanded matters were also covered.
issues.conclusion: For a pre-2003 assessment that is not finalized, or is pending in an appeal before the District Judge, the assessee may request assessment on the annual-value basis; if requested, the matter is to be determined under that method.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 116G(2) and 169(1), third proviso, of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, as amended in 2003, permit an assessee to seek determination on the basis of annual value when an assessment was not finalized or a covered appeal was pending. “Annual value” is defined by section 2(1A), and section 116E supplies the unit-area method for its determination. The third proviso to section 169 requires transfer of a pending District Judge appeal to the Municipal Taxation Tribunal upon the applicant’s request; “settlement” in that proviso means determination by the Tribunal, not a consensual settlement. The Court affirmed the interpretation in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Major General Inderpal Singh Kahai & Anr.

rule.if: property_tax_assessment_proceeding and pre_change_assessment and (assessment_unfinalized_or_remanded or district_judge_appeal_pending) and assessee_requests_annual_value_basis

predicates.property_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns assessment of property tax on land or a building.
predicates.pre_change_assessment: The assessment concerns a period before the new annual-value method took effect.
predicates.assessment_unfinalized_or_remanded: The assessment had not become final, including because it had been set aside or remanded for fresh determination.
predicates.district_judge_appeal_pending: An appeal concerning the assessment was pending before a District Judge.
predicates.assessee_requests_annual_value_basis: The assessee asked for the assessment or appeal to be determined on the basis of annual value.

issues.definition: If a pre-change property-tax assessment is unresolved or has a covered appeal pending, and the assessee requests the annual-value basis, the assessment must be determined on that basis.
